Simulate multiple fisheries with user-supplied allocations

Source: R/sim_programs.R
sim_fisheries.Rd

Declares all fisheries upfront and interleaves their operations, using one population and one age-specific mortality budget per replicate and year.

sim_fisheries(sim, ..., n_sims = NULL)

Arguments

sim

A simulation list returned by sim_distribution().

...

Named sim_fishery_spec configurations made with sim_fishery() without its sim argument. Names must be unique and nonempty.

n_sims

Common replicate count; NULL inherits existing batch metadata, otherwise one. Do not supply counts inside configurations.

Value

The simulation list with replicates and combined fishery results as described by sim_fishery(). Fishery identifiers distinguish catches, operations, spatial removals and annual CPUE; effort units are never pooled. The mortality ledger and population are shared across fisheries.

Details

All fisheries inherit the weight relationship stored by sim_abundance(). Weights belong to the population, not individual programs.

Every fishery's reference target uses the original population and Z. At each age/year the sum of fishery_share * mean_selectivity_at_age must not exceed one. Incompatible configurations produce an error rather than being normalized. Integer targets are rounded jointly across fisheries, preserving the rounded combined target and overall mortality bound.

At each operation the next active fishery is chosen uniformly. Catches deplete shared age-length stocks and death budgets. A fishery retires on reaching its target, exhausting accessible catching opportunities, or reaching its operation limit. Shared stocks and access restrictions can constrain valid allocations. Other deaths are allocated once, after all fishing. Interleaving defines operation order, not calendar time. All truth precedes reporting and biological sampling.

Configurations are processed in canonical name order, so registration order does not affect same-seed results. Randomness uses the caller's RNG state. Calling this function again runs a fresh scenario from the original annual population; it replaces the fishery results, rather than appending removals. Future annual populations are not changed. See sim_fishery() for capture, monitoring, units, and the conditional interpretation of effort and CPUE.

See also

vignette("fisheries", package = "SimSurvey") for the joint workflow and a mathematical appendix.

Examples

trawl <- sim_fishery(fishery_share = 0.2, catch_model = sim_capture(q = 0.1))
gillnet <- sim_fishery(fishery_share = 0.1, catch_model = sim_capture(q = 0.05))
# population |> sim_fisheries(trawl = trawl, gillnet = gillnet)
